name: Kanchenjunga Base Camp Trek (North and South Base Camps Circuit)
sub_region: Taplejung District, Koshi Province; Kanchenjunga Conservation Area

difficulty.notes: Long, remote teahouse/camping circuit; high point Pangpema (North Base Camp, approx. 5,143 m) on a day hike; one long multi-pass day (Sele La, Sinion La, Mirgin La, approx. 4,290-4,500 m) between the north and south sides.

duration_days.basis: Full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu, including Kathmandu-Bhadrapur flights and drives to/from Taplejung
duration_days.notes: North-only or south-only versions run approx. 16-18 days. Road extensions now allow drives beyond Taplejung (e.g. to Sekathum/Lelep) on some itineraries, shortening the walk-in. Some itineraries end at Khebang/Khamdime by jeep.

itinerary.notes: Ilam altitude quoted 1,200-1,627 m by operators.
Some itineraries overnight at Sekathum (approx. 1,660 m) instead.
Largest village on the route; one source gives 3,415 m.

itinerary.route: Lhonak - Pangpema (North Base Camp, approx. 5,143 m) - Lhonak
itinerary.notes: Close views of Kanchenjunga north face and glacier.

itinerary.route: Cross Sele La, Sinion La and Mirgin La - Cheram (Tseram)
itinerary.notes: Longest day; views of Jannu and Makalu.

itinerary.route: Ramche - Oktang viewpoint (South Base Camp side, approx. 4,730 m) - Cheram
itinerary.notes: Yalung glacier and south face views. Some itineraries return to Ramche instead.
Some itineraries split this into two days.

itinerary.route: Khebang - drive to Bhadrapur (or via Taplejung)

best_seasons.notes: Spring (rhododendrons) and autumn (clear views) per operator guidance; passes can be snowbound in winter and trails leech-infested and landslide-prone in monsoon.

permits.name: Kanchenjunga Restricted Area Permit (Taplejung: Phaktanglung RM wards 6-7, Mikwakhola RM ward 5, Sirijunga RM ward 8)
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week for the first 4 weeks; USD 25 per person per week beyond 4 weeks

permits.name: Kanchenjunga Conservation Area entry (KCA / KCAP)
permits.fee: NPR 2,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 500)

permits.name: TIMS card (agency-issued)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals; Kanchenjunga routes are on the NTB guide-and-TIMS list

guide_requirements: Restricted area: permit through a registered trekking agency with a licensed trekking guide. Since 22 March 2026 solo trekkers may obtain restricted-area permits (two-person minimum removed), max 7 trekkers per guide. Kanchenjunga Base Camp routes are also on the NTB list requiring a licensed guide and agency TIMS.

flights: Alternative: Kathmandu - Biratnagar - Suketar (Taplejung) where operating
drives: Bhadrapur - Ilam - Taplejung (approx. 2 days, or 1 long day)
logistics.notes: Basic teahouses now exist along most of the circuit; camping may be needed in places or in shoulder seasons.

highlights: Pangpema, Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (approx. 5,143 m)
Oktang viewpoint and Yalung glacier below the south face
Sele La / Sinion La / Mirgin La crossing
Tibetan-influenced Ghunsa and Limbu/Rai villages in the lower valleys
Kanchenjunga Conservation Area wildlife (red panda, snow leopard habitat)
risks: Landslide sections between Ghunsa and Khambachen
Snow on Sele La passes outside main season

acclimatization.notes: Two acclimatization days before Lhonak/Pangpema are standard on 22+ day itineraries.

unverified: Ghunsa altitude: 3,595 m in most sources, 3,415 m in one.
Tortong/Torongding altitude: 2,995 m in most sources, 2,080 m in one.

South Base Camp naming: trekkers' 'South Base Camp' is usually the Oktang viewpoint (approx. 4,730 m); one source gives Yalung Bar 4,500 m; the climbing base camp on the Yalung glacier is approx. 5,475-5,500 m.
Pangpema altitude 5,143 m is widely quoted by operators; not confirmed by an official source.
